text:
Anya: Pushed a new compact right-rail layout for autoscale controls. Trying to fit Pool, SLO, Max/Min steppers, Burst toggle, and a tiny cost hint without making it look cramped. PTAL and flag any accessibility or copy issues. Link to Figma in PR.
Priya: Nice work shrinking it down. Quick thought: when space is tight, users still expect Max to be the primary control. Make Max visually heavier and place it before Min in the tab order.
Marco: Re: pool selector 97 dropdown with 50 pools is a mess. I suggest a searchable modal triggered from the rail with grouping by region and small badges for "Ada/Nvidia" and "cost tier". Also add an "auto-recommend" pill that picks the pool based on latency footprint.
Kevin: Accessibility checklist incoming. Top items: 1) Pool selector must be role=dialog and trap focus, 2) steppers need clear aria-labels ("Max instances", "Min instances"), 3) SLO slider should have aria-describedby pointing to a live region for explanations, 4) burst toggle must be keyboard focusable with aria-checked state.
Jen: Microcopy: change label from just "Burst" to "Burst (temporary)" and tooltip: "Temporary instances that scale down automatically; billed while active." Also propose the SLO helper line: "Higher SLO = lower failure risk; Lower SLO = cost savings." Keep it <100 chars.
Anya: UX question: cost hint small inline vs. hovering cost preview? Wanted inline so designers can iterate quickly. Thoughts?
Priya: Inline is better for experimentation. Show subtle text: "(est +1.9% cost)" next to Max value. Click opens full cost modal.
Marco: Implementation note: client can estimate delta using current workload profile. We'll emit autoscale.preview events and include workload_id so server can reproduce numbers.
Kevin: Also add aria-live announcer for numeric updates so screen reader users hear: "Max set to 12, est +1.9% cost". Use aria-live="polite" on a sibling element that updates.
UX-research: From 7 remote sessions with the compact rail: 5 users tried to adjust Max first. Even with labels, visual weight matters. Recommend bold Max label, lighter Min. Also users disliked hidden burst: they want burst visible with clear temporary language.
Jen: Guardrail copy: if SLO <45 show orange note: "Warn: <45% may increase throttles" and if user tries <30 block and show: "Minimum allowed SLO is 30% due to backend limits."
Anya: Good call. Backend enforces min_slo=30. Let's reflect that.
Marco: Event names I'll add to the PR: autoscale.open, autoscale.change_max, autoscale.change_min, autoscale.toggle_burst, autoscale.select_pool, autoscale.set_slo, autoscale.preview. Each event should carry {user_id, session_id, prev, new, ui_slot}.
Kevin: Keyboard order proposal for compact rail: Pool button -> SLO slider -> Max stepper -> Min stepper -> Burst toggle -> Save. That keeps primary inflight controls early. Confirm with UX-research.
UX-research: Confirmed. Users preferred Pool and SLO near the top for quick routing checks.
Jen: I'll land the microcopy branch once Marco adds events. Tiny tooltip copy is in the PR already.
Anya: @Marco can you add the telemetry schema? @Kevin please paste the short a11y checklist into the PR so designers can mark items done. @UX-research can you add two quote snippets to the thread for context?
Marco: Will add telemetry schema and sample payloads.
Kevin: Checklist (short): role=dialog for pool modal; focus trap; aria-labels for steppers and slider; aria-describedby for SLO explaining tradeoffs; aria-live announcer for changes; aria-pressed/aria-selected on pool rows; keyboard order validated; visible focus styles high-contrast. I'll add code snippets in PR.
UX-research: Two quotes to include: 1) "I always reach for Max first94that's my mental model of capacity." 2) "Burst should say temporary right on the toggle; otherwise I assume it's permanent."
deploy-bot: Design review thread created 90180999000090 (DR-3551). Reviewers: @product-team. Link: https://jira/redwood/DR-3551
Anya: Thanks everyone 94 I'll merge after Marco/Kevin's updates. If we get objections I'll hold until morning.
